speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your sudden choking, forceful coughing after retching, and severe chest pain following heavy alcohol use, I suspect a tear in your esophagus. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray and REQUEST IMAGES of your chest cavity.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray findings show free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation. Physical examination reveals fullness at the base of the neck, a crunching and rasping sound (Hamman's sign) on auscultation, and possible crepitus on palpation of the chest and neck. Vital signs indicate tachycardia (107 bpm) and borderline hypotension (90/68 mmHg).

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the X-ray showing free mediastinal air and the physical exam revealing Hamman's sign, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).
